title: Fall of a branch start and level-independent fall

key_results.statement: Zeroth-order velocity of a branch start, exact and constant in $\lambda$: $v^{(0)}=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g$.

First-order velocity, exact for all $\lambda\ge0$: $v^{(1)}(\lambda)=\lambda\langle a_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g+\rho(\lambda)$, with $\rho(\lambda)=\rho_\infty+\sigma\operatorname{Re}\int\frac{dp}{2\pi}e^{2i\sigma\omega\lambda}R_\sigma(p)$ and $\rho_\infty=\sigma\int\frac{dp}{2\pi}B_\parallel'\xi_g$.

Secular coefficient and drift acceleration for every label: $a_{k,\sigma}(p)=\frac{g_{\zeta,k}\tau_k^4\sin^2p-G_kM_k\tau_k^2\cos2p}{\omega_k^2}+\sigma\mathcal F_k\frac{\tau_k^2(M_k^2\cos2p-\tau_k^2\sin^4p)}{\omega_k^3}$, with $|a_{k,\sigma}|\le\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}\mathsf b_k$.

The rest is bounded for all $\lambda\ge0$ (exact): $|\rho(\lambda)|\le\frac{\tau}{M}\mathsf b(3X_g+\frac{\tau}{2M})$ and $|\rho(\lambda)-\rho_\infty|\le\frac{\tau}{M}\mathsf b(X_g+\frac{\tau}{2M})$; it converges to $\rho_\infty$ like $\lambda^{-1/2}$ (order estimate).

Remainder beyond first order on the chain $|x|\le L$, exact for all $\lambda\ge0$: $|v_L-v_L^{(0)}-v_L^{(1)}|\le2\tau L^2\mathsf b'(\lambda^2\mathsf b'+\lambda|g_\zeta|)$; it is not uniform in $L$ and grows with $\lambda$.

Window average of the first-order acceleration at fixed $g$: $|\overline{a^{(1)}}-\langle a_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g|\le\frac{2\tau}{M\Lambda}\mathsf b(X_g+\frac{\tau}{2M})$ (exact), so the long-window limit is $\langle a_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g$.

The drift acceleration (long window, then sharp label) exists for every $p_0$ and equals $a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$, with $|\langle a_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g-a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)|\le\frac12\sup|a_{k,\sigma}''|\,\delta p^2$ (exact).

Sharp-label limit of the first-order acceleration at fixed $\lambda$ for a family centred at $x_c$: $a_{k,\sigma}-A_\sigma\cos(2\omega\lambda)+2\omega\theta'B_\perp(\omega'\lambda+\sigma x_c)\sin(2\omega\lambda)$ at $p=p_0$.

The limits of a long window and of a sharp label commute if and only if $(G_k-g_{\zeta,k}M_k)\sin^2(2p_0)=0$, in particular at rest; otherwise the order sharp label first has no limit and the window average oscillates between $a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)\pm|n_k(p_0)|$.

Branch start at rest, sharp label: $\bar x^{(1)}_{\rm lab}(\lambda)-\bar x_{\rm lab}(0)=\frac12a_{k,\sigma}(0)\lambda^2-\sigma\frac{\tau^2\mathcal F}{2M^3}\sin^2(M\lambda)$; the term $\lambda\sin(2M\lambda)$ of the bare start and the $G$, $g_\zeta$ parts of its oscillation are absent.
Drift acceleration at rest: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\sigma\mathcal F_k-G_k)$.

In the drift velocity $v=\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)$: $a_{k,\sigma}=\frac{\tau^2}{M}(\sigma\mathcal F-G)+c_{2,k,\sigma}v^2+O(v^4)$ with $c_{2,k,\sigma}=g_\zeta+\frac GM(1+\frac{2M^2}{\tau^2})-\sigma\frac{\mathcal F}{M}(\frac32+\frac{2M^2}{\tau^2})$.

In well-defined quantities of the effective body contract: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\sigma\frac{8\bar t_k^2}{\Delta_k}\delta E^\sigma_k$ and $c_{2,k,\sigma}=\frac{\delta t_k}{\bar t_k}+\frac{\delta\Delta_k}{\Delta_k}(1+\frac{\Delta_k^2}{8\bar t_k^2})+\sigma\frac{\delta E^+_k+\delta E^-_k}{\Delta_k}(\frac32+\frac{\Delta_k^2}{8\bar t_k^2})$, invariant under the replacements (8.1).

From rest: $a_{k,+}(0)$ is level-independent iff $\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_k-G_k)$ is; $a_{k,-}(0)$ iff $\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_k+G_k)$ is; both with the same value $a$ iff $\mathcal F_k=0$ and $\tau_k^2G_k/M_k=-a$ for all $k$.

Upper branch through the order $v^2$, exactly: $\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_k-G_k)=a_0$ for all $k$ and $g_{\zeta,k}-\frac{\mathcal F_k}{2M_k}-\frac{a_0}{\tau_k^2}(1+\frac{2M_k^2}{\tau_k^2})$ independent of $k$.

For $M_k\ll\tau_k$ at leading order: the same first condition and $g_{\zeta,k}-\frac{\mathcal F_k}{2M_k}-\frac{a_0}{\tau_k^2}$ independent of $k$; the dropped lattice terms are $-2a_0M_k^2/\tau_k^4$, of relative order $M_k^2/\tau_k^2$.

Class $\mathcal C$, every $N\ge2$: $a_{k,+}(0)$ is level-independent iff $\mathcal F=m(g_m-g_\eta)$, $a_{k,-}(0)$ iff $\mathcal F=-m(g_m-g_\eta)$, with the value $-\tau^2g_\eta$ in each case; both iff $\mathcal F=0$ and $g_m=g_\eta$.

Class $\mathcal C$ through the order $v^2$: for $N=2$, $\mathcal F=m(g_m-g_\eta)=-\frac{4g_\eta}{\tau^2}m(m+\frac{\pi}{\lambda_0})(2m+\frac{\pi}{\lambda_0})$; for $N\ge3$, $g_m=g_\eta=0$ and $\mathcal F=0$; at leading order in $M_k/\tau$ for every $N\ge2$, $\mathcal F=0$ and $g_m=g_\eta$; $g_\zeta$ is free in all three.

If the fall from rest is level-independent and not zero (either branch): $\frac{d^2\bar x}{d\lambda^2}=-\frac{v_{\max}^2}{d_0}\frac{r(x+1)-r(x)}{r(x)}\hat e$ at first order in the gradients, without $m$, $N$, $\lambda_0$, the level $k$ or $\mathcal F$.

Variants: (a) and (c) fall with $-\tau^2g$ for all levels in both branches and are level-independent through $v^2$ only at leading order in $M_k/\tau$; (b1), (b2), (d) and (f) with $c_{\rm f}\neq0$ depend on the level already at rest.

open_issues: The second order in the gradients is not derived; the remainder bound (4.9) is not uniform in L and grows with λ, so (4.7) is an acceleration of the first-order coefficient, not a statement about long falls.
The sharp-label limit at fixed λ (4.13) is derived for centred families of starts; families that are not centred are not classified.
The constants in O(v^4) of (4.17), in the supremum of the second derivative in (4.11) and in the λ^(-1/2) decay of the rest are not made explicit.
Item 4 uses the rate (3.23) in its wide-start form, defined at zeroth order in the gradients; the comparison of two clocks inside one description is left to 05-rate-comparison.
Records beyond leading order in κ and starts in a superposition of levels or branches are outside the scope.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of (4.7), (4.17), (4.24) and the case of all gradients zero (constant velocity, no first-order term).
Upper branch at rest reproduces a_sec of (3.15) and (3.28); the branch-weighted sum of a_{k,σ}(p) reproduces a_sec(p) of (3.26) for all p; the F oscillation of (4.15) equals that of (3.15).
Conjugation with σ2 maps the upper branch to the lower branch with F → −F and λ → −λ, in agreement with (4.7); for τ_k → 0 the acceleration and the velocity vanish.
